title.narrative: Strengthening Protection for Women, Girls, and Vulnerable Populations impacted by the conflict in Sudan through Integrated GBV, Shelter, and Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance interventions in Gedaref

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtAccording to the IOM DTM Flash Report, between 20 October and 28 November 2024, it is estimated that a total of 393,337 individuals (78,963HHs) were displaced from various locations within Aj Jazirah due to intensified hostilities between SAF and RSF. Approximately 41% of the IDPs have sought refuge in Gedaref, (Madeinat Al Gedaref (49,720 IDPs) ltugtand Al Butanah (35,105 IDPs)lt/ugt). Among the individuals who have been displaced, it is estimated that 16,930 had already been displaced before the escalation. Significant protection concerns have been raised, as reports are indicating the separation of IDPs from their family members, incidents of plundering, and occurrences of sexual and gender-based violence (GBV). The primary requirements of most displaced individuals in Gedaref include access to food, adequate shelter, secure drinking water, sanitation facilities, and health and protection services. ltbrgtIn response to the above needs, the IRC aims to provide support to 16,389 individuals through GBV, shelter, and MPCA interventions. the IRC aims to improve the protective environment for adolescent girls and strengthen community structures in preventing and responding to GBV through a community-based approach that connects women and girls to specialized services by leveraging its multi-sectoral interventions. In partnership with a local organization, the IRC will also enhance its capacity to deliver timely and dignified Child Protection (CP) services, aligning with the SHF’s localization agenda.ltbrgtIRC and AMVO will provide structured and context-specific psychosocial support (PSS) interventions for women and girls at temporary Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS). Additionally, the IRC will implement its Girl Shine curriculum, to empower, protect, and support adolescent girls in humanitarian contexts. ltbrgtThe IRC will train its AMVo staff on case management, GBV concepts, guiding principles, and safe referral mechanisms. Furthermore, frontline GBV actors and community structures will receive training on fundamental GBV concepts and minimum standards. As part of GBV risk mitigation efforts, the IRC and its partner will distribute dignity packages to vulnerable women and girls, including Persons with Specific Needs (PSN), women-headed households, and persons with disability, and conduct quarterly safety audits. Community involvement will be fostered through FGDs with men, boys, women, and girls to assess risks, raise awareness, and observe GBV-related issues. These efforts aim to establish secure and supportive communities where women can reach their full potential.ltbrgtUnder shelter and NFIs, the IRC, through its partner JASMAR, will provide immediate relief to IDPs by establishing 15 communal shelters and distributing 1190 non-food items (NFIs) and 200 emergency shelter kits These distributions will address urgent shelter and basic needs, alleviating hardships caused by the conflict. Coordination with local authorities and community leaders will ensure equitable access and effective aid delivery. Given the heightened GBV risks faced by IDPs, particularly women and girls, the IRC’s response will be closely integrated with its protection team. Distribution points will be carefully chosen to prioritize safety, ensuring women and girls can access services without fear of violence. The shelter kits and hygiene items will be designed to enhance privacy, security, and dignity, reducing GBV exposure. Additionally, 250 HHs will be selected to receive MPCA support. ltbrgtThe IRC will implement a MEAL plan, incorporating field visits, regular reporting, and post-distribution monitoring (PDM). Additionally, a CFM will be established in collaboration with the protection team to allow beneficiaries, especially those at risk of GBV, to report concerns and receive timely responses safely. This integrated approach will strengthen affected communities' safety, well-being, and empowerment while ensuring gender-sensitive service delivery. ltbrgtlt/pgt
